comments.text: I would say that the name of the country is UK 🇬🇧, since they have a seat at the UN. 🇺🇳 England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿, Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿, Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿 and Northern Ireland don’t have a seat at the UN, they don’t have their own currency, military, foreign policy and they have to follow the laws set by the UK government. The only reason that they are called countries is that the people living in England and Scotland for example are more proud of that region than the UK as a whole. Their nationalism is connected to their region and not the country as a whole. England, Scotland and Wales used to be separate countries a long time ago, but they are not countries now. If you ask ChatGPT about this, it will boil down to this: people use two different meanings of the word country. When people say that England is a country, they don’t mean country as in the US, Germany, Finland, China and so on. It’s a different meaning, almost like a different word. Like one word can have different meanings, you know.

comments.author: @petercannell2963
comments.text:
The Isle of Man is a country with a constitutional monarchy as part of a sovereign parliament, Tynwald.  The legal currency is the Manx Pound which is tied to sterling.  The lieutenant governor is the King’s representative.  We share a monarch with the UK but are not part of nor ever has been part of the UK.  

Charles Windsor’s title on the Isle of Man is “Lord of Mann” but would more accurately be “King of Mann & the Isles”.  

Its mainland is Mannanan.  It’s next largest Island of the archipelago that makes up the “Isle of Man” is the Calf.  There are others.  

Hope this is of interest.
